la:verb:intueor.gloss: to look at, upon or towards
senses: to look at, upon or towards
to consider, regard, observe, give attention to, contemplate
to regard with admiration, admire, wonder at, stare
la:verb:intueor.html:
in-tŭĕor, ĭtus, 2, v. dep. (in tmesi:
inque tueri,; archaic form indo tuetur, Enn. ap. = Ann. 73 Vahl.; and intuor,; ; Turp. ap. ; , and in the act. form intŭo, ĕre, ; ), to look at, upon, or towards (syn.: adspicio, contemplor, specto).
Lit., constr. with simple acc., or in and acc.
With simple acc.: terram intuens modeste,: solem,; : aliquid oculis,: ornamenta rei publicae,: cum intueor et contemplor unumquemque vestrum,: huc atque illuc,: lasciviam piscium, Pac. ap. : terram,: me omnes intueri,: ora omnium atque oculos,: quid, ut noverca, me intueris?: faciem alicujus,: caelum,: nutum illius diligenter,to watch,.— Of situation: cubiculum montes intuentur,.—
With in and acc.: in speciem rerum intuens,: in te intuens,.—
Trop.
Of the mind, to regard, observe, contemplate, consider, give attention to.
With acc. (so most freq.): ut tota mente Crassum atque omni animo intueretur,; cf.: intentis oculis omnes rei publicae partes,: voluntatem eorum qui audiunt,: mentis acies seipsam intuens,: oratores,: potius, quid se facere par esset, intuebatur, quam quid alii laudaturi forent. he regarded more, had more respect for, ; cf. : rationem,; : tempestatem impendentem,: id ille intuens,. — In pass. part.: intuendum quid affectet quisque,: non tam veteranos intuendos nobis,.—
With adv.: quo intuens,.—
With in and acc.: in summos homines,: tu in tuā mtuens te continebis,: in aliquod majus malum,; ; .—
With ad (rare): ad finiendum bellum,.—
Esp., to regard with admiration, admire, wonder at: Graeci sic te intuebuntur, ut quendam ex annalium memoria esse delapsum putent,: sicut aliquem de caelo delapsum,.?*! intueri, in pass. sense, .

senses: from within, from the inside, out
la:adv:intus.html:
intus, adv.
1. in and the abl. termination -tus; Sanscr. -tas; cf. ἐντός
.
On the inside, within: ibi intro atque intus subducam ratiunculam,: vide sitne istaec nostra intus,: intus insidiae sunt: intus inclusum periculum est: intus est hostis,: estne frater intus?: intus domique,: ea, quae sunt intus in corpore,; cf.: intus in mundo,: intus in animis,; so, intus in cella Fortis Fortunae,: te intus et in cute novi,: extra et mtus hostem habere,.— Poet., with abl.: membris intus,: tali intus templo,.— With gen.: aedium,i.e. in the house,: adductos intus agere equos,closer to the goal,; cf.: intus agere lacrimas,to moderate,.—Prov.: intus canere, v. Aspendius.—
To the inside, into, within, in (for the usual intro, cf. ): intus novam nuptam deduxi viā, rectā,into the house, dub. (al. intro): die, me orare ut aliquis intus prodeat,: quo simul atque intus est itum, (al. intro): intus in artus,; ; : pollice intus inclinato, inwards ( = introrsus), ; so . —
From within = ἔνδοθεν, ex interiore parte (mostly anteclass.; cf. Brix ad ): tu in tus pateram proferto foras,: evocato aliquem intus ad te,; ; ; ; cf.: intus evocato aliquem foras,; and: argentum intus efferre foras,: obsera otium intus,: quicquid spinosum est et intus eminet,.

la:verb:intumesco.html:
in-tŭmesco, mŭi, 3,
v. n. inch., to swell up; to rise (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit.: fluctus flatu intumescens,; : vidi virgineas intumuisse genas,.— Of dropsical persons: intumuit suffusā venter ab undā,: si partes corporis in vesicas intumuerint,.—
Transf., to rise, be elevated, of the surface of the ground: loco tamen ipso paululum intumescente,; cf.: nec intumescit alta viperis humus,.—
Trop.
To swell up: vox intumescit,: motus,grows, increases,: intumuere statim superbia ferociaque,: jure quodam potestatis intumescere,to be puffed up, elated,: rebus secundis,: supra humanum modum,.—
To become angry: intumuit vati,: Juno, quod, etc.,;
